domain: Political Theory / International Relations / Territorial Sovereignty
topic_summary: Analysis of competing legitimacy claims over Israel/Palestine territory. Research reveals two potentially distinct kernels: 1948 existential legitimacy (Israel's right to exist vs Palestinian displacement) and 1967 territorial boundaries (occupation vs self-determination). The dispute conflates these kernels at elite/institutional level while grassroots actors show partial shared substrate recognition.

key_entities: State of Israel (established 1948, claims divine promise and refuge narrative)
Palestinian Authority/PLO (governance in West Bank, claims autochthony and displacement narrative)
Hamas (governance in Gaza, rejectionist position on 1948)
United States (primary diplomatic patron of Israel)
UN (observer status for PLO 1974, Resolution 181 partition plan)
1948 refugees and descendants (core of Palestinian narrative)
key_tensions: Autochthony vs divine promise (first possession vs God-given land)
1948 legitimacy vs displacement (Israel's existence vs Nakba)
Memory vs memory (persecution-survival narrative vs displacement-loss narrative)
key_mechanisms: Narrative selectivity (each side omits own contribution, demonizes other)
Conflation of 1948 and 1967 grievances (valorizes own victimization, denies other's legitimacy)
Historical revisionism (excludes other from continuity claims when national identity hinges on millennia-long presence)
key_absences: Grassroots coexistence frameworks (research notes individual-level shared substrate recognition not reflected in elite positions)
Distinction between moderate and extremist positions (conflation mechanism obscures this boundary)

commitment_system_recognition.kernel_description: Two distinct but conflated kernels: (1) 1948 existential legitimacy kernel (right to statehood vs displacement), (2) 1967 territorial boundaries kernel (occupation vs self-determination). Elite/institutional actors treat as mutually exclusive; grassroots shows partial shared substrate.
commitment_system_recognition.authority_description: Competing authority structures: Israeli state claims Balfour Declaration + UN 181 + divine promise; Palestinian claims autochthony + UNRWA refugee status + UN observer recognition. No shared interpretive authority.

axiom_contradictions.basis: Zionist reading holds Israeli statehood as legitimate response to persecution with Palestinian displacement as regrettable but secondary; Palestinian reading holds displacement as primary injustice requiring remedy through right of return. No framework can simultaneously hold both 'Israeli statehood legitimately established 1948' and 'Palestinian displacement delegitimizes 1948 state formation' as foundational axioms.

Coexistence reading accepts permanence of 1948 state formation and limits right of return to future Palestinian state; autochthony reading treats right of return to 1948 territories as non-negotiable. No framework can hold both 'right of return must be limited to enable coexistence' and 'right of return to original homes is foundational and non-negotiable.'

omegas.description: Research finding: dispute contains TWO distinct kernels (1948 existential legitimacy, 1967 territorial boundaries) conflated at elite level but partially separated at grassroots. This is a structural finding about the dispute itself, not a generation failure. The conflation mechanism may itself warrant separate analysis.
omegas.source: §1.3-K kernel recognition + research context on 1948/1967 disentanglement

omegas.description: Grassroots actors show partial shared substrate recognition (dual entitlement) not reflected in elite/institutional positions. This divergence may indicate that the axiom contradictions are elite-constructed rather than inherent to the dispute. Deferred axis grassroots_shared_substrate captures this.
omegas.source: Deferred axis grassroots_shared_substrate + research on individual-level dual entitlement

omegas.description: Two-state coexistence reading has coexists_with edge to both maximalist readings AND axiom contradictions with palestinian_autochthony_reading. This is licensed plurality: socially live position holding axioms that contradict another live position. Does this indicate the dispute is structurally resolvable via institutional design, or does it merely defer the contradiction?

Research notes religion as 'bright boundary' implying ultimate truth and heresy framing. Does this make the divine promise component of zionist_refuge_reading non-negotiable even within moderate Israeli frameworks? If so, the coexistence reading may be structurally unstable.
omegas.source: Extraction anchor on religion as bright boundary + zionist_refuge_reading authority grounding

omegas.description: Right of return appears in palestinian_autochthony_reading as non-negotiable and in two_state_coexistence_reading as limited to Palestinian state. Is this a rope (coordination problem) or snare (one reading's core demand structurally forecloses the other)? Epsilon classification may shift based on demographic projections.
omegas.source: Axiom contradiction between autochthony and coexistence readings + extraction anchor on right of return as demographic threat
